key_insight: Reward models inherit value and preference biases from their LLM pretraining: even after supervised or preference fine-tuning, RMs display systematic differences in moral, social, and value judgments that reflect their initialization.
problem_solved: Clarifies how pretraining shapes downstream reward models and quantifies the degree to which inherited representations produce biased value judgments—filling a gap in RM auditing and alignment research.
method: Assembled 10 leading open-weight reward models initialized from different pretrained LLMs.
Evaluated RMs using validated psycholinguistic and moral judgment corpora to probe value, moral, and social preference signals.
Performed comparative analyses (score distributions, effect sizes, and correlations) to attribute observed differences to pretraining initialization rather than only to fine-tuning.
impact: Highlights that RM initialization matters for alignment and fairness: practitioners must audit and account for pretrained biases when training or deploying reward models to avoid unintended value transfer and misaligned behavior.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing bias/value scores across the 10 RMs for key psycholinguistic tests (side-by-side bars per test).
Heatmap showing correlation between pretrained model features (e.g., corpus/source or architecture) and RM bias dimensions.
Pipeline diagram: Pretrained LLM → RM initialization → Fine-tuning → Observed value biases, with callouts showing where inherited effects emerge.
Example prompt-response tiles illustrating divergent RM preference scores on the same moral/social question.
paper_title: Reward Models Inherit Value Biases from Pretraining
paper_authors: Brian Christian, Jessica A. F. Thompson, Elle Michelle Yang, Vincent Adam, Hannah Rose Kirk
